marrow__ANAT_CH36_Q015.takeaway: Whitlow can compromise the distal four-fifths of the terminal phalanx, while the proximal fifth is spared by the pulp septal arterial pattern.
marrow__ANAT_CH36_Q015.displayText: The image shows an infection of the pulp space of a finger, or whitlow. It requires incision and drainage because, if neglected, it can lead to necrosis of the distal 4/5th of the terminal phalanx. It does not cause necrosis of the entire phalanx because the proximal 1/5th is spared where the artery does not cross the fibrous septa. The pulp space contains subcutaneous fat arranged in tight compartments formed by fibrous septa from skin to periosteum. Complications include ischemic necrosis of the distal 4/5th of the terminal phalanx, osteomyelitis, flexor tenosynovitis and septic arthritis of the distal interphalangeal joint.

rationales.b: Osteomyelitis is a recognized complication of untreated pulp-space infection.
rationales.c: Infection can spread to the flexor tendon sheath and cause tenosynovitis.
rationales.d: Septic arthritis of the distal interphalangeal joint is also a listed complication.
